_comment: Mission «Корона 1. Грюнвальд, 1410» (mission card in the missions doc, docs/03-missions/12-crown_01_grunwald_1410.md). A field battle without a base on the field of «ВКЛ 2» (map_crown_01 is map_gdl_02 with the oak grove behind the Polish left wing). Player 1 is Jaśko of Łęczyca and the banners of the left wing; player 2 the Order; allies (setup.sides) 3 the Kraków banner and the centre with the great banner of the kingdom (Marcin of Wrocimowice) and Zyndram, 4 the Lithuanian wing, 5 the king on his hill with Oleśnicki and the guard. Rules in core/mission/mission_field.gd (rules.field): the heat on men in heavy armour, the line nobody crosses before the order, the great banner and the guest knights taken for ransom. Read by core/mission/mission_def.gd; cells are map cells, ticks 1/20 s, texts are English keys translated through i18n/*.po.
title: Crown 1. Grunwald, 1410

briefing.place: The field between Grunwald, Stębark and Ludwikowo, Prussia. 15 July 1410.
briefing.story: The armies of King Władysław Jagiełło and Grand Duke Vytautas stand against the Order of Grand Master Ulrich von Jungingen. The Poles hold the left wing, the Lithuanians the right. Jaśko of Łęczyca, twenty-two years old, in borrowed armour on a borrowed horse, waits with the lances of the left wing in the shade of a grove, while the Order stands in the sun.
briefing.goal: Wait for the order, then hold the blow of the Order's right wing. When the great banner of the kingdom falls, raise it. Do not let the Grand Master's reserve reach the king, and take the wagenburg together with the Lithuanians.
lose: The king is killed or taken
The great banner of the kingdom lies on the ground longer than 60 seconds
Jaśko's banners are cut to pieces

do.text: The king has fallen. The army has lost its head.
Jaśko is struck from his horse and carried off the field.
The great banner of the kingdom lies in the dust. The Polish banners waver and break.
Jaśko's banners have been cut to pieces.

lines: Pan Jan of Łęczyca told me at Orsha about his great-grandfather Jaśko. That day Jaśko was twenty-two years old, the armour on him was another man's, and his horse was borrowed. Ours stood in the grove, the Germans stood in the sun, and the king was still hearing Mass.
The second Mass. If the Germans roast in their pots before noon, there will be nobody left for us to fight.
Let them roast. My horse is borrowed, I am in no hurry.
King! The Master sends you a sword, if you are short of your own. And if you are cramped, we will draw back and give you the field.
We have swords enough. But this one I will take, and let God be the judge. Nor will we look for a field: such as the Lord has sent us, on that we shall stand.
To horse! We go at the signal, not before. Whoever jumps out first for glory, the Germans will take first.
The old men argued afterwards who led ours then: the sword-bearer Zyndram or the marshal. Jaśko remembered Zyndram, because he shouted louder than anyone.

do.text: Wait for the order and do not ride out before it
Set up wayside crosses on all 3 places of power
Take a guest knight captive
It is hot. Lances in the sun tire and lose heart; in the shade of the grove and in the wet hollows they rest. The Order has stood in the sun since morning. Do not hurry.
The priest can set up a wayside cross on a place of power. Each cross gives Power for «Bogurodzica».

lines: Stand! Who stuck his nose out there? Back into the shade, let them bake.
Mother sang this over the flax. I never thought men went to die to it.

do.text: Throw back the blow of the Order's right wing
A knight's lance strikes hardest at a gallop over open ground. After the blow pull it back and charge again: in a long melee the lance loses its edge.
«Bogurodzica»: the priest sings and the spirit of everyone around rises; the fleeing turn back. The first time it was sung by itself, from now on it costs Power.
A guest knight has given himself up. His ransom will be paid in silver.

lines: The Lithuanians have run! They have left us here alone!
Run, or led the Germans away after them, we will sort that out later. Now close up on the left, there is a gap there.
In the middle of the Polish line the white eagle sways over the press, leans and is gone. For a moment it is quiet. The Order's knights shout something joyful.
The banner! After me, whoever is in the saddle!

do.text: Raise the fallen banner of the kingdom
Raise the banner in under 30 seconds
The banner lies on the ground: %s
Bring Jaśko to the fallen banner within 60 seconds. While it is down, the whole Polish army has lost the spirit it gave.

lines: The shaft is pinned down by a dead horse. Jaśko jumps from the saddle and pulls; it will not come. Beside him a hand in a red sleeve takes hold of the shaft. A man without armour, in a red kaftan, with merry eyes. The fight seems to flow around him.
Heavy, sir knight? Let us do it together. We will settle up later.
The banner rises. All along the line the Poles roar. Jaśko looks round: there is nobody in red beside him.
Many hands raised the banner, and whose, nobody wrote down. Pan Jan insisted that one of them was his great-grandfather's. And of the other, in the red sleeve, his family did not like to speak.

do.text: Jaśko has «The Pact». Once in this mission: for 30 seconds the units around him lose no spirit and strike harder. It costs no Power. What it costs, you will learn later.
Do not let the Grand Master's reserve reach the king
The Grand Master leads his reserve round our wing, at the king's hill. Two fresh banners from the king's reserve have come up by Stębark. Keep men by the king, do not throw everything into the fight.

lines: The king's hill. A lone knight of the Order with his lance lowered rides straight at Jagiełło. A young scribe without armour catches up a broken lance and strikes the knight in the side; he falls. The king strikes him with his own lance, the guard finishes him.
That scribe was Zbigniew Oleśnicki, later a cardinal. And the German Długosz calls Dypold Kökeritz of Lusatia. I am a scribe myself and love this story more than any other.
Look, on the right! The Lithuanians!
So now we know. Forward, before the Master looks round!
The Master is down! Killed in the press!
To the wagons! Strike their wagenburg before they come to their senses!

do.text: Take the wagenburg together with the Lithuanians
The broken banners of the Order hold out behind the chained wagons by Grunwald. Break in and cut them down.

lines: Evening. The broken wagenburg. One wagon is full of iron fetters. Jaśko takes a pair in his hands.
They brought these for us. They knew how it would end.
They did not know. They thought they knew.
In the dusk behind the wagon a red kaftan flickers. Jaśko goes there, but there is only a strange carter in a rust-coloured shirt.

The Master was found among the dead, with wounds in the forehead and the chest. The next day the king had the body sent to Malbork. And all his life Jaśko looked for the man in red, to ask how much he owed. He found him forty-four years later.

do.text: The Order is beaten at Grunwald.
